tone_statements.citation: Cao, Xiaolan (Amy). 2018. Southern Pinghua: phonology and phonological diversity. Proceedings of the 51st International Conference on Sino-Tibetan Languages and Linguistics (ICSTLL 51), Kyoto University, 22 pp. (presentation slides).http://hdl.handle.net/2433/235266
tone_statements.quote: Figure 8 cross-speaker average tone contours of the Wucun Dialect • The Wucun dialect has three level tonemes (high, mid, and low), two falling tonemes (high and low), and one rising toneme • In comparison, the Shangyao dialect has four level tonemes (high, mid, low, and extra low), one falling toneme, and two rising tonemes (high and low) (de Sousa (2011)) • Phonetic tone contours vary considerably across Southern Pinghua dialects. Nevertheless, they can be divided roughly into two distinctive groups based on the number of rising tonemes.

tone_statements.citation: de Sousa, Hilário. 2017 [online 2016]. Pínghuà 平話 Dialects (Pinghua of Guangxi). In Rint Sybesma, Wolfgang Behr, Yueguo Gu, Zev Handel, C.-T. James Huang & James Myers (eds.), Encyclopedia of Chinese Language and Linguistics, vol. 3, 425-431. Leiden: Brill. [read in the author's open pre-publication draft dated 2012-08-20, 16 pp.]
tone_statements.quote: The phonology of Southern Pínghuà bears similarities with Cantonese and many other Yuè dialects: it is relatively conservative in retaining all six ancient codas -m -n -ŋ -p -t -k, and there are at least three entering (rù 入) tones. ... – Split in one or both entering tones; most Pínghuà dialects have a split of the entering tone based on vowel length/quality like Yuè dialects. However, in the Pínghuà dialects of Nánníng and places upriver, it is the lower-register entering tone (yángrù 陽入) that is split, based on whether the initial is sonorant or obstruent in Middle Chinese, e.g., Nánníng Shàngyáo /hip23/ 葉 'leaf' (< *jep) ... versus /hak2/ 學 'learn' ... – No systematic tone-sandhi.
tone_statements.locator: author's draft (2012-08-20) p. 1 (introduction) and pp. 4-5 (list of Southern Pinghua phonological traits); published version ECLL vol. 3: 425-431
tone_statements.summary: Tonal Sinitic language of the Yue-Pinghua type: MC tone categories split by register; Southern Pinghua retains checked syllables with at least three entering tones; in Nanning-type dialects the lower entering tone splits by historical initial sonority (e.g. 23 vs 2) rather than vowel length; no systematic tone sandhi in Southern Pinghua. (Full inventory per held Cao 2018 slides: Wucun 6 unchecked…

tone_statements.citation: de Sousa, Hilário. 2016. Language contact in Nanning: Nanning Pinghua and Nanning Cantonese. In Hilary M. Chappell (ed.), Diversity in Sinitic Languages, 155-189. Oxford: OUP.
tone_statements.quote: The phonologies of Nanning Pinghua, Nanning Cantonese and Standard Cantonese share many similarities: they all have at least six tonemes, the stop codas of -p -t -k -m -n -ŋ ... Nanning Pinghua and the other Yongjiang type of Southern Pinghua also have one of their Entering tones, the Lower Entering tone, split into two. However, the conditioning factor in Nanning Pinghua is different from Yue and Zhuang; the conditioning factor is whether the initial in Middle Chinese is a sonorant ... or an obstruent. ... Vowel length plays no role in the splitting of the Entering tone in Nanning Pinghua.
tone_statements.locator: author's draft (2014-03-03), section 2 'Phonology', draft p. 15 (six tonemes) and pp. 21-22 (third phonological trait: Entering-tone split); published OUP chapter pp. 157-189
tone_statements.summary: At least six tonemes (unchecked) plus entering (checked) tones; Lower Entering tone split in two by the Middle Chinese initial's sonority (23 vs 2), not by vowel length; syllable = tone-bearing unit (CGVX+T template); no statement on stress or sandhi in the passage read.
